# Hypothesis Testing in ML

Hypothesis testing governs A/B testing, model comparison, feature selection, and the interpretation of benchmark improvements. Misunderstanding p-values is extremely common — this note builds the correct mental model.

## The Framework

H₀ (null): no effect / status quo. H₁ (alternative): the claim to support.

**Procedure**: compute test statistic T(D), compute p-value = P(T≥t_obs | H₀), reject H₀ if p ≤ α.

We never prove H₁ — we either reject H₀ or fail to (insufficient evidence ≠ evidence for H₀).

## P-value — Definition and Misconceptions

**p-value = P(T ≥ t_obs | H₀)** — probability of data at least this extreme if H₀ were true.

NOT: P(H₀ is true | data). NOT: P(results due to chance). NOT: effect size.

## Type I and Type II Errors

| | H₀ True | H₀ False |
|---|---|---|
| Reject H₀ | **Type I (α)** — False Positive | Correct (**Power = 1−β**) |
| Fail to Reject | Correct | **Type II (β)** — False Negative |

Power increases with effect size δ, sample size n, and significance level α.

Sample size per group: n = 2(z_{α/2} + z_β)² σ²/δ² ≈ 16σ²/δ² for α=0.05, power=80%.

## Common Tests in ML

- **t-test**: compare means; T = (x̄−μ₀)/(s/√n) ~ t(n−1)
- **Chi-squared test**: categorical independence; T = Σ(O−E)²/E ~ χ²(df)
- **Permutation test**: reshuffle labels, build empirical null — no distributional assumptions; gold standard for model comparison

## Multiple Testing Problem

m tests at α=0.05: P(at least one FP) ≈ mα. For m=20: ~64% chance of false positive.

- **Bonferroni**: use α/m per test — controls FWER, conservative
- **Benjamini-Hochberg**: controls FDR = E[FP/(FP+TP)]; sort p-values, reject k largest below kq/m threshold

```python
# Two-sample t-test for model comparison
t_stat, p_val = stats.ttest_ind(model_a, model_b, alternative='less')

# Permutation test (model-agnostic)
obs_diff = model_b.mean() - model_a.mean()
perm_p = sum(perm_diff >= obs_diff for _ in range(10000)) / 10000

# Bonferroni correction
bonferroni_reject = p_values < alpha / m
```

## A/B Testing in ML

**Stopping rules**: peeking and stopping when p<0.05 inflates Type I error. Use:
- Fixed horizon: decide n upfront, test once
- Sequential analysis (SPRT, mSPRT): valid at every point
- Bayesian A/B: stop when P(μ_B > μ_A) > threshold

**Practical vs statistical significance**: large n makes tiny effects significant. Always report effect size (Cohen's d, relative lift) alongside p-values.

## Confidence Intervals as Duals

H₀: θ=θ₀ is rejected at α iff θ₀ ∉ 95% CI. CIs communicate effect size and uncertainty — report them instead of p-values alone.
